cards.text: There's been no rain for a long time, and the famine is severe in Samaria. Now the LORD has told Elijah, His prophet, that He will send rain. Elijah has told Ahab, king of Israel, to gather all Israel on Mount Carmel, along with the prophets of Baal and Asherah.
So Ahab summons all the Israelites and assembles the prophets on Mount Carmel. Friend, when the boss calls the WHOLE company into one room at once, nobody walks in thinking it's raise day.

Elijah walks right up to all the people with a question: "How long will you waver between two opinions?" Friend, that's somebody standing with one foot on each side of a fence for so long they forgot which yard is theirs.

cards.question: Elijah asks the people how long they'll waver between two opinions. What does he want them to do?

answers.text: Decide who is God and follow
Keep both gods just to be safe
Wait and see what happens next

cards.question: When Elijah challenges them to choose, the people shout back their answer right away.

cards.text: Then Elijah lays out the numbers: he's the only remaining prophet of the LORD, and Baal has four hundred and fifty. Friend, if I walked into a meeting and it was me against four hundred and fifty, I'd say I was looking for the restroom and hop RIGHT back out.
So Elijah sets up a test with two bulls. Baal's prophets will choose one, cut it into pieces and put it on the wood, and Elijah will do the same with the other.

cards.question: Both sides will put a bull on the wood. What is the one thing neither side is allowed to do?
Each side will call on its god. Elijah says the God who answers by ___, He is God.
The people stayed silent at Elijah's first question, but when he lays out the fire test, they answer and say his plan is good.
Since the prophets of Baal are so numerous, Elijah tells them to choose a bull and prepare it first.

cards.text: So they prepare their bull and start calling on Baal, shouting, "O Baal, answer us!" They keep it up from morning until noon, leaping around the altar they made.

cards.question: The prophets of Baal shout and leap around their altar from morning until noon. What answer do they get?

cards.text: At noon, Elijah starts to taunt them: "Shout louder, for he is a god!" Friend, that's the prophet version of "Did you try unplugging it and plugging it back in?"

cards.question: Elijah keeps taunting: maybe Baal is deep in thought, or occupied, or on a journey, or sleeping. Any reason at all he hasn't ___ them.
After Elijah's taunt, the prophets of Baal give up and go quiet.

cards.text: Not even close. They shout louder and cut themselves with knives and lances, as was their custom, until the blood gushes over them.

cards.question: Midday passes, and the prophets of Baal keep on raving. How long do they keep going?

cards.text: And still, no response: no one answered, no one paid attention. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and I heard more back there than they heard all day.
Now it's Elijah's turn. He says to all the people, "Come near to me." So they all come close.

cards.question: There's an altar of the LORD on the mountain, but it had been torn down. What does Elijah do with it?

answers.text: He tells Ahab to fix it

cards.text: Then Elijah picks up stones. Twelve of them, friend. Not eleven, not thirteen.

cards.question: Why does Elijah take exactly twelve stones for the LORD's altar?

answers.text: One for each tribe of Jacob's sons
One for each month of the year
One for each man helping him

cards.text: Jacob is the one the word of the LORD came to, saying, "Israel shall be your name." With those stones, Elijah builds an altar in the name of the LORD.
Then he digs a trench around the altar, big enough to hold two seahs of seed. He arranges the wood, cuts up the bull and lays it on top.

cards.question: Elijah's bull is on the wood, all set for fire. Then he has them pour ___ on the offering and the wood.
Elijah has them fill four waterpots and pour them on the offering and the wood, then do it a second time, and then a third time.

cards.text: So the water runs down around the altar and even fills the trench. Friend, I've seen bakers do some WILD things, but NOBODY pours water in the oven right before they want it hot.
At the time of the evening sacrifice, Elijah the prophet steps up to the altar and prays to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel.

cards.question: Elijah prays at the altar. What does he ask the LORD to let be known this day?

answers.text: That He is God in Israel

cards.question: Elijah asks the LORD to answer so the people will know He is God and that He has turned their hearts back again.
When the fire of the LORD falls on Elijah's soaked altar, it burns up the bull but leaves the stones and the trench water behind.

cards.text: The sacrifice, the wood, the stones, the dust, and it licks up the water in the trench. Friend, I've burned a batch or two in my day, but I have NEVER burned the cookie sheet, the counter AND the dish water.

cards.question: Earlier, the people didn't answer Elijah a word. Now they've seen the fire of the LORD. What do they do?

answers.text: Fall facedown and say the LORD is God
Run down the mountain in fear

cards.text: Facedown, all of them: "The LORD, He is God! The LORD, He is God!" The same crowd that didn't answer a word before.
Then Elijah gives the people an order: "Seize the prophets of Baal! Do not let a single one escape."

cards.question: The people ignore Elijah's order and let the prophets of Baal get away.

cards.text: They seize them, and Elijah brings them down to the Kishon Valley and slaughters them there.

cards.question: Then Elijah turns to Ahab. What does he say he can hear?

answers.text: The sound of a heavy rain

cards.text: Elijah tells Ahab to go up, eat and drink. So Ahab goes up to eat and drink.

cards.question: Ahab goes up to eat and drink, but Elijah climbs to the summit of Carmel. What does Elijah do up there?

answers.text: Bends down with his face between his knees
Builds a second altar to the LORD
Lights a big fire to signal Ahab

cards.text: "Go and look toward the sea," he tells his servant. The servant goes, looks, and reports back: "There is nothing there."

cards.question: When the servant sees nothing, Elijah calls it off and heads down the mountain.

cards.text: Seven times, Elijah says, "Go back." Friend, that's me cracking the oven door again and again and AGAIN, waiting for the cookies to rise.

cards.question: On the seventh time, the servant finally sees something rising from the sea: a ___ as small as a man's hand.
One tiny cloud, and Elijah sends his servant with a message for Ahab. What does it say?

answers.text: Get your chariot and go before the rain stops you
Stay up on the mountain until the storm passes
Bring the people back for another sacrifice

cards.text: Meanwhile, the sky grows dark with clouds and wind, and a heavy rain begins to fall. A cloud the size of a hand, and then THIS, friend.

cards.question: Ahab rides away as the heavy rain falls, and he goes to ___.
The hand of the LORD comes upon Elijah, and he rides to Jezreel in Ahab's chariot.

cards.text: He tucks his cloak into his belt and runs ahead of Ahab all the way to Jezreel. Friend, I stand on a gold base, so I can't even outrun a cookie rolling off the counter.
And that's where we'll let this batch cool for now. Keep your apron on, friend, because Elijah's story isn't finished yet.
